open_obligations: Note that finding more flaws and choosing correct solutions are different outcomes.
Check difficulty: hard contest code versus the answers critiqued in Saunders et al.
Check the size of McAleese et al.'s appendix experiment.

Note that McAleese et al.'s contractors judged without access to code execution, and that the authors suspect the negative result came from the asymmetry between the compute needed to find the solutions and the compute used to produce the critiques; check whether critic compute was scaled in this experiment.
in.other_title: LLM critics did not help humans pick correct solutions to hard contest-style coding problems
in.rationale: Saunders et al. report critique assistance helps labelers find about 50% more critiques of model- or human-written answers. McAleese et al. report broadly negative results when measuring human judge accuracy directly on hard competition-code problems: LLM critiques struggled to help contractors identify the correct solution within 20 minutes; the outcome measure (choosing the correct solution versus counting flaws found) and domain differ.
in.scope: proposed CHALLENGES: whether model-written critiques improve human evaluation outcomes

text: The paper reports that human labelers asked to find critiques of model- or human-written answers find about 50% more critiques when given assistance from a critique model, and that with deliberately misleading answers, assisted labelers find the intended critiques 50% more often.
title: Critique assistance: labelers find about 50% more critiques of summaries
